title: openai-compat: add seed/determinism + metadata passthrough for Responses API variants and stabilize streaming/structured output
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: The Responses-style endpoints in our OpenAI compatibility layer lacked explicit support for seed/determinism flags and did not consistently preserve user-provided metadata across streaming events, tool/function-calling events, and the final structured output. This caused regressions in downstream evals and made deterministic replay difficult for customers relying on seed-based determinism.

This PR implements: 1) seed and determinism passthrough from the OpenAI Responses request surface into the inference adapter (mapping to our runtime temperature/seed inputs and a deterministic execution path where supported); 2) metadata passthrough so that the top-level request metadata (user-supplied fields and SDK/console tags) are propagated into all streaming event frames and emitted tool-call events; 3) structured output stability: we ensure tool/function-call events include metadata and that final response objects include the exact metadata envelope received; 4) fixes to streaming framing to avoid final-frame races (race observed in integration tests under heavy load); 5) updated docs and migration notes for the OpenAI compatibility guide.

Implementation notes: - Added seed/determinism keys handling to redwood/openai_compat/responses_adapter.py with conservative mapping (seed -> runtime seed, determinism true -> force low-variance decoding heuristics where supported). - Streaming path (redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py) now attaches a metadata header to each event frame and emits a terminal 'response.complete' event only after the kv cache flush and application-level finalizers succeed. - Tool/function calling wrappers were updated to copy metadata into tool events and to preserve the original call_id for traceability. - Integration tests added to redwood/openai_compat/tests to cover seed reproducibility, metadata propagation, and structured output shape. - Documentation updated under redwood-docs/openai-compat/responses.md with migration guidance and examples.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Default behaviour preserves existing semantics when seed/determinism fields are absent. Where determinism is requested but the underlying runtime does not support strict deterministic decoding on a given model, we fall back to the best-effort low-variance mode and emit a warning in the response metadata. This is surfaced in the compatibility docs and via an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers.

Testing: Unit tests cover mapping logic and edge cases. Integration tests run against the local canary runtime and a mocked backend to assert that metadata appears in streaming frames, tool events, and final responses. CI flakiness observed in earlier runs (integration-tests) was resolved by adding a small backpressure delay in the stream finalizer and by tightening the test harness timeouts.

Related: ENG-1294 (determinism roadmap), ENG-1320 (streaming stability). Supports SUP-402 reproducer.

Migration: No forced customer action required. Customers who rely on exact deterministic replay should opt into the "deterministic_compat" flag in the OpenAI compatibility layer and validate results for their model+runtime combination.

Release notes summary: Adds seed/determinism flags support and metadata passthrough for Responses API variants; stabilizes streaming finalization and structured output to include request metadata.

fix(streaming): ensure metadata is included in all streaming event frames and avoid final-frame races
feat(tool-calls): propagate metadata and preserve call_id for tool/function events
test: add integration tests for seed reproducibility and metadata propagation
docs(openai-compat): update Responses docs and migration guide

merge_commit_summary: openai-compat: seed/determinism + metadata passthrough for Responses variants; stabilize streaming and structured output
release_notes:
- Adds seed/determinism flags support to OpenAI Responses compatibility layer.
- Preserves user/request metadata across streaming frames, tool/function-call events, and final structured responses.
- Streaming finalization made more robust to avoid race conditions under heavy load.
- No breaking behavioral changes when fields are absent; deterministic mode is opt-in and best-effort where runtime support is limited.
notes_for_release_manager: Verify that dedicated customers who opt into deterministic_compat are informed; consider a short internal rollout to Dedicated customers before general availability.
